newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia plans to speed up privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia plans to speed up privatisations.

text.p: Tunisia plans to privatise 15 more public firms before the end of 1996, bringing the total number of companies privatised during the year to 29, Economic Development Minister Taoufik Baccar said on Tuesday.
He told journalists that so far in 1996 the government has also liquidated five public firms and sold a minority stake in a further three companies.

Baccar said that of the total of 135 government-owned firms, about 60 had been earmarked for privatisation, with the rest to be kept in the public sector for the time being because of their strategic importance.
The state also owns minority stakes in a further 300 other companies.

Baccar did not name the firms to be privatised, but said that their activities were in non-strategic sectors. Last month officials said that the firms soon to privatised include five state-owned cement companies.

Official sources told Reuters the government plans to privatise 62 companies over the next few years, mainly in the ceramics, cement, food and textile sectors, and it expects to raise some $1.4 billion from their sale.
Last year 14 public firms were fully privatised and minority stakes sold in three others through public share offers. In 1994 five companies were privatised,
Baccar said that since 1992 revenues from privatisations amounted to 300 million dinars ($310 million), most of which was invested in restructuring other public companies.
He said the government plans to involve merchant banks in carrying out future privatisations.
There is only one merchant bank based in Tunisia -- International Merchant Bank.

In August Tunisia formed a a central state body to speed up its slow-moving privatisation effort. A new department was set up at the Ministry of Economic Development to formulate and propose privatisation programmes for final approval by an existing ministerial committee chaired by the Prime Minister and called CAREPP.
A junior minister at the Economic Development Ministry, Moncef Ben Abdallah, was named this year to manage the programme. ($=0.97 dinar)
